Notarized power of attorney for incorporation representatives

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (CSSF) anti-money laundering guidance, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EU Regulation 2580/2001 and EU Regulation 833/2014), the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and domestic Luxembourg politically exposed persons (PEP) database. Enhanced due diligence mandatory for any PEP, sanctioned entity, or entity from high-risk third countries as identified by FATF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be submitted in French or German transliteration into Latin characters. Use of the local language is not mandatory, but the name must be distinguishable from all existing trade names in the Luxembourg trade and companies register (RCS). If using non-Latin script, a French or German transliteration is required. The name must comply with Luxembourg naming conventions and may not be contrary to public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may within one month from the date of the refusal submit a written administrative appeal to the Minister of Justice via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR). The appeal must set out the legal grounds for challenge and include all relevant supporting documentation. An extension of the name reservation may be requested prior to expiry by submitting the renewal request through the LBR online portal; the extension is normally granted for an additional 30-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For ISIC 6201 (Cloud Document Automation and E-Signature Authentication), a virtual office is generally permissible provided that the registered office is a physical address in Luxembourg where statutory records are maintained and where official correspondence and judicial documents can be served. The Commercial Code requires the registered office to be a real address; a virtual office may be accepted for administrative correspondence but must not be solely used for incorporation without any physical presence. However, the Luxembourg tax administration may scrutinize virtual offices for substance requirements under the substantial presence doctrine for tax residency and VAT grouping.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% — Standard low-risk profile for a LegalTech SaaS entity with no regulated activities; unannounced inspections are uncommon but possible if irregularities arise in filings or if the entity is selected for a random compliance audit by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register or tax authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Chapter 5 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', Articles 710-1 to 710-26; Articles 26-1 et seq. (corporate purpose), Article 1795-5 (RCS publication), and the Law of 3 September 2013 on business establishment permits.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and accessible through the eJustice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of incorporation (Acte constitutif) filed by a Luxembourg notary with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 for a SARL, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution and are released only after RCS registration of the notarial deed; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF LU SARL: ADOPTED by the Board of Managers on [DATE]. WHEREAS the share capital of EUR 12,000 has been fully subscribed and paid up into the blocked account of the company at [BANK], and the notarial deed of incorporation has been executed. RESOLVED FIRST, that the subscription of EUR 12,000 divided into 100 shares of EUR 120 each is ratified and accepted. RESOLVED SECOND, that the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], L-[XXXX] [CITY], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED THIRD, that [NAME] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole signature power. RESOLVED FOURTH, that the Manager is authorized to complete RCS registration, VAT registration, business establishment permit application, bank account opening, and all beneficial ownership filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and negative certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request to the RCS through the LBR e-suite, specifying the proposed corporate name 'LU SARL' with up to three alternative names, the intended corporate purpose and the name of the appointed notary. The RCS examines the proposed denomination against existing registered companies and issues a negative certificate (certificat de non-confusion) confirming the name is not confusingly similar. The reservation is valid for two months and may be renewed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and alternative names
Detailed corporate purpose description
Identification documents of founding shareholders
Appointed notary's name and reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity or public policy grounds, propose an amended denomination and resubmit the reservation; a court appeal is available to the competent district court if the RCS maintains the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and deposit of minimum share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution duly authorized by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the name of the company 'in formation' with a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the full minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 into a blocked account (compte bloqué). The bank issues a certificate of capital blocking and payment, which is a pre-requisite for the notarial deed. The funds remain blocked until RCS registration of the company and are automatically released to the company on presentation of the RCS certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Negative certificate issued by the RCS
Identification and KYC documents of all signatories and beneficial owners
Bank account opening application forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional anti-money-laundering documentation, promptly deliver source-of-funds evidence and a completed beneficial ownership register draft; if the bank delays, open the account with another CSSF-authorized Luxembourg credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Notaire) with practice in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the final draft articles of association, the bank blocking certificate and the required declarations to the notary. The notary verifies the legality of the corporate purpose, the full subscription and payment of the share capital, and the integrity and capacity of each manager in accordance with Article 710-12 of the 1915 Law. All founders and the first manager appear before the notary to sign the authentic deed. The same deed contains the acceptance of office by the manager and determines the signature powers of the company.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Negative certificate from the RCS
Bank capital blocking certificate
Valid identity documents of each shareholder
Declaration on honour of non-conviction for each manager (extrait du casier judiciaire)
Written acceptance of office signed by the first manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect, amend the statutory clauses and re-execute the deed; if the certificate of non-conviction is outstanding, obtain the judicial record from the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice or from the competent foreign authority before the notary date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the LBR electronic filing system; publication by the Official Journal in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following execution, the notary electronically transmits the incorporation deed, the list of subscribed shares, the managers' declarations, and proof of the registered office consent to the RCS. The RCS verifies the compliance of the filing, enters the company in the register, assigns the RCS registration number, and forwards the file for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Legal personality commences on completion of the RCS registration; the RESA publication is a publicity requirement.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Bank certificate confirming the release of capital
Consent of the registered office owner
Manager candidacy acceptance and non-conviction declarations
Notary's transmission certificate and accompanying schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS suspends the registration or issues a query, the notary files additional documents or rectified declarations through the LBR portal; completion of the filing cures the default and registration proceeds once all conditions are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes, Department of Business Establishment Permits (service via MyGuichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the mandatory Autorisation d'établissement covering the activity of computer programming and software publishing (ISIC 6201) under the Law of 3 September 2013. Lodge the online application through MyGuichet.lu with proof of the professional integrity and competence of the manager, the RCS registration extract, and proof of commercial premises. The permit is issued for each business location and must be kept available for inspection at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Application form for the business establishment permit
Extract of criminal record for each manager
Diplomas, certificates or evidence of professional competence in IT services
RCS registration certificate (extract)
Proof of occupancy or lease of the business premises
Identification documents of the permit applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused, submit a written reconsideration request with supplementary evidence of professional qualifications; an appeal may be filed with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security and beneficial ownership declarations; workplace clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE register); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); local communal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Luxembourg VAT through the MyGuichet.lu portal using standard registration forms, supplying the RCS certification and predicted annual turnover. Enroll the company and its personnel with the CCSS for social security and labour declarations. File the beneficial owner declaration in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) held by the LBR. Notify the ITM of the workplace, and obtain fire safety clearance for the occupied premises from the local commune and fire brigade. The company may then lawfully invoice and commence operations.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of incorporation
Notarial deed of incorporation and managers' declarations
VAT registration forms and supporting turnover estimate
Beneficial ownership declaration with ownership details
Occupancy, fire safety and structural compliance documents
ITM workplace registration and health and safety assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is delayed, follow up through the AEDT and submit the request for urgent processing; if the RBE filing is queried, correct and resubmit within the statutory deadline; any ITM or fire-safety deficiency must be remediated and re-inspected before lawful occupation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes, Business Establishment Permit Department, in coordination with the local Commune for building, fire and occupancy permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) issued under the Law of 3 September 2013 on the authorization of commercial, craft, industrial and certain independent activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based IT and SaaS activities are not listed in the mandatory or screening annexes of the Law of 27 May 2022 on environmental impact assessments; no full EIA report and no EIA registration are required for the described LegalTech SaaS operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharges, VOC emissions or industrial waste streams arise from a standard office and data processing environment. The company must nevertheless comply with the Grand-Ducal regulation on waste management (Law of 21 March 2017, as amended), including proper separate collection of e-waste under the WEEE Directive transposition, and with municipal sanitary and storm-water regulations. If the office workforce exceeds the statutory threshold, energy-efficiency reporting under Luxembourg's energy consumption rules applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of the registered office is required under the Grand-Ducal regulation of 24 November 2008 on fire prevention and rescue in buildings (avord technique), issued by the local commune based on the fire brigade's (Service d'Incendie et de Secours) inspection. Structural load inspection of the leased premises must be certified by the building owner and submitted with the occupancy permit. Workplace clearance must be obtained from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) confirming compliance with Articles L.311-1 to L.312-4 of the Luxembourg Labor Code, covering ventilation, lighting, sanitary facilities, electrical installations and emergency evacuation routes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SARL is incorporated through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via MyGuichet. The commercial registration automatically generates the national business registration number. For VAT, an application is submitted to the AEDT using the MyGuichet portal and the RCS corporate file; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) and the ACD assigns a direct tax dossier number. A non-established foreign entity may apply directly for VAT registration by filing AEDT Form 640 with supporting evidence of Luxembourg taxable activity, legal establishment, and if applicable a tax representative appointment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or transparent-classification election exists under Luxembourg law; an SARL is per se an opaque taxable corporate entity subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. Available elections include group taxation under Article 164bis LIR for resident corporate taxpayers (binding for five consecutive years) and opt-in participation-exemption treatment for qualifying shareholdings. Hybrid mismatch elections are prohibited because Luxembourg has implemented ATAD I and ATAD II with mandatory no-double-counting and anti-reverse-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual net turnover for the small-business exemption under Article 64 of the Luxembourg VAT law; exceeding this threshold triggers mandatory VAT registration for a Luxembourg SARL. Non-established suppliers of any Luxembourg-taxable services or distance sales have no benefit of the small-business threshold and are registrable from their first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance or tax-authority pre-approval regime applies to B2B/B2C VAT invoices in Luxembourg. B2G e-invoicing has been mandatory for public-sector contracts since 1 May 2022, requiring structured electronic invoices compliant with European Standard EN 16931 exchanged via the Peppol BIS 3.0 network. VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and listing declarations are submitted electronically through the AEDT ELMA portal; no API tax stamping or invoice clearance API is currently imposed for private invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rate applies to (1) direct export of goods from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union when the supplier holds a valid customs export declaration and transport documentation; (2) intra-EU supplies of goods dispatched to another Member State in favour of a VAT-registered customer whose valid VAT identification number appears on the invoice and the corresponding recapitulative statement is filed; and (3) qualifying ancillary export services and certain cross-border services supplied to customers outside Luxembourg where the place-of-supply rules place the service outside the territory. The supplier must maintain complete documentary proof before and after the declaration; failure to substantiate the movement or the transfer of ownership triggers VAT reassessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic export declaration in the Luxembourg customs ACE system)
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR waybill, or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, the supplier's and customer's purchase/sales contracts
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 transfer proving receipt of payment in foreign currency
Valid VAT identification number of the EU customer and the corresponding Intra-Community recapitulative statement for intra-EU dispatch
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities and customs authorities audit export zero-rating retrospectively with strict documentary scrutiny. Where export evidence is incomplete, incorrect, or inconsistent with the transport route, the VAT initially zero-rated is clawed back retroactively with late-payment interest and administrative fines, typically up to EUR 20,000 per taxable operation or per offending invoice. In cases of deliberately false declarations, forged export documents, or fraudulent abuse of an export chain, criminal tax fraud proceedings may be initiated, yielding fines of up to four times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years. VAT records and export substantiation must be retained for a minimum of six years in accordance with Luxembourg VAT retention rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the Central Bank of the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg; monetary authority for the euro area is the European Central Bank (ECB) in Frankfurt, and the BCL is a Eurosystem member. The BCL operates the national payment clearing infrastructure (LIPS and participation in TARGET2/T2) and is the national compiler of balance-of-payments (BoP) statistics. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the prudential supervisor of credit institutions, electronic money institutions and payment service providers. There is no separate foreign-exchange control administration in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full eurozone member; the euro is fully and freely convertible, and there are no exchange-control restrictions. Both current-account and capital-account movements are liberalised under Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and transposed Luxembourg law. No prior BCL or CSSF authorisation is required for inbound share capital, outbound dividends, liquidation proceeds, interest, SaaS subscription fees or royalty remittances. The only impediments are tax-based, not convertibility-based: a 15% domestic dividend withholding tax rate (mitigable to 5% or 0% under double tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive); no Luxembourg interest withholding tax for corporate payees; and no Luxembourg royalty withholding tax for non-resident corporate recipients. Multi-currency bank accounts are freely permitted, and foreign currency may be retained onshore or offshore without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export-proceeds surrender requirements in Luxembourg. No statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation obligation applies to export earnings, including proceeds from cloud-based legal automation and e-signature services delivered under ISIC 6201. The sole formal duty is statistical: under the Luxembourg Law of 22 June 1999 and implementing BCL balance-of-payments regulations, resident credit institutions and other collecting agents report cross-border transactions equal to or exceeding the applicable BCL threshold (generally EUR 12,500) to the BCL for BoP compilation. The company must provide its bank with an accurate purpose code and remittance description so that the bank can file the necessary return. No export licence, conversion certificate, or central-bank approval is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE), Luxembourg

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into Luxembourg under the revised Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366; Low for offshore digital EMIs without an EU/EEA licence. An offshore EMI (for example, a US or post-Brexit UK entity without a Luxembourg branch or without a passporting notification filed with the CSSF) cannot lawfully hold resident corporate funds as a payment account in Luxembourg; reliance on such an entity creates unregulated-activity risk, sanctions-screening gaps, and no access to the Luxembourg Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGDL) protection of EUR 100,000, which covers only credit institutions. EU-licensed EMIs such as Stripe, Airwallex, MangoPay and Currence may be onboarded for inbound card and SEPA collections, but the treasury policy must require: (i) that EMI balances are safeguarded client funds and are not treated as bank deposits; (ii) an automatic daily sweep of all balances above a defined cap (for example EUR 50,000) to a tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution; and (iii) a formal agreement designating the EMI as a payments collector, not a treasury depository. Stripe, as an Irish payment institution, is commercially viable for card acquiring, but the Luxembourg SARL remains the merchant of record and must provide full UBO, VIES, incorporation and transaction-forecast documentation at onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Luxembourg tier-1 banks expect at least one face-to-face or video-verified interview with the managing director or a duly authorised signatory before opening a corporate account. Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, the bank must positively identify the entity, its directors and its ultimate beneficial owners. A physical presence at the bank's premises in Luxembourg is not always mandatory; a CSSF-compliant video-identification session using eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures is accepted by BIL and BNP Paribas for low-risk corporates, subject to submission of notarised or apostilled corporate documents. For non-resident directors, the most reliable route is hybrid: (i) the managing director appears once before a Luxembourg notary during incorporation, which eliminates apostille requirements for EU public documents under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191; (ii) the bank accepts the notarially certified mandate and certified copies of passports; and (iii) ongoing signatories onboard remotely with video KYC and eIDAS signing where the bank's CDD policy permits. Remote-only opening remains the exception and, for a LegalTech SaaS SARL, is attainable with pre-existing bank relationships or a banking-as-a-service introducer, but it cannot be assumed across all tier-1 banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: ultimate beneficial owners are non-EU residents or hold their interest through a chain of holding companies, making the natural-person ownership unclear to the compliance officer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) an RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) registration transcript issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers; (ii) a signed UBO declaration under the Law of 10 July 2020 showing the full ownership chain to each natural person with percentage holdings; (iii) certified passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; (iv) a notarially certified power of attorney for the authorised signatory; (v) recent bank reference letters and documented source of capital (shareholder bank statements bridging the capital contribution); and (vi) a written group-structure memorandum explaining the commercial rationale for the Luxembourg SARL and its SaaS operating model, contradicting any shell-company inference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: the unlicensed, online LegalTech business model processes cross-border card payments through Stripe, creating a perception of high-volume, low-touch transactions with elevated anonymous-settlement and potential sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) a statutory licence-exemption memorandum confirming that no banking, EMI, or payment-services licence is required because the company delivers software services (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541199) rather than financial services; (ii) an internal AML/CTF compliance playbook containing an entity-level risk assessment classifying the business as Low Risk Standard; (iii) corporate governance documentation (articles of association, shareholder register, signed customer agreements, privacy and e-signature policies); (iv) a funds-flow diagram showing card acquiring through the EMI followed by a daily sweep to a Luxembourg bank account; (v) PCI-DSS and SOC 2 Type II attestations confirming that card data is held by the payment provider; and (vi) a negative sanctions/PEP/adverse-media screening report on the entity, its directors and UBOs, with a defined screening-refresh policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: name-screening hits against EU/UN/OFAC/UK sanctions lists, PEP status, or adverse-media database entries that, if unresolved, trigger automatic account refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) a formal screening-disambiguation memo containing the exact screening run, timestamp, and an analysis discarding homonyms and false positives; (ii) a PEP declaration and, where applicable, a proportionate enhanced due-diligence file for any genuinely identified PEP; (iii) a legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour confirming that no designated person owns or controls the SARL and that the capital injection is lawful; and (iv) documentary proof of the source of funds, including shareholder resolutions approving the capital call, bank statements evidencing liquidity, and the corresponding SWIFT purpose codes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the statutory minimum capital of EUR 12,000 required for a Luxembourg SARL: (1) the bank opens a blocked capital account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation and issues a consignation attestation to the Luxembourg notary; (2) the foreign shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 with field 50K (ordering customer), field 59A (beneficiary SARL account), field 33B (EUR amount), and field 70 stating 'INVESTMENT / SHARE CAPITAL INJECTION / LU SARL / RCS LUXEMBOURG', using the ISO 20022 External Purpose Code 'CBFF' (capital building) or 'INVS' (investment) supplemented by BPM6 direct-investment classification D.3; (3) if the transfer originates inside SEPA, the bank prefers a SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) carrying the same purpose code; (4) the bank releases the blocked-account attestation only after final value is credited in EUR with no conditional or reversible credit; (5) the notary files the deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and the funds become freely operable after registration; (6) for a post-incorporation capital increase, the same CBFF-coded SWIFT rail is used, supported by a notarised shareholders' resolution and updated RBE filing. No BCL authorisation, FX approval, or central-bank permit is required, but the purpose code and contract documentation must be retained to satisfy CSSF record-keeping and BCL BoP reporting obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR-denominated operating disbursements (cloud hosting, subcontractors, software licences, employee salaries) are cleared through TARGET2/LIPS via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for standard payments and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for pan-EU sub-second settlement; for non-EUR or non-SEPA payments, SWIFT MT103 is the standard rail, with correct purpose codes, beneficiary bank identifiers, and pre-submission screening against EU/OFAC/UN sanctions. For high-value cross-border trade requiring documentary settlements, the company may use Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700), complemented by presentation documents (commercial invoice, proof of electronic delivery or transport document, insurance certificate) and, where required, a confirming bank; performance guarantees may be issued as standby letters of credit under SWIFT MT760. The card-acquiring outbound leg is executed through Stripe, which settles daily to the Luxembourg operational account via SEPA or instant SEPA, with chargeback and dispute handling managed through the Stripe Dashboard/API. To maintain the audit trail required by CSSF, every FX conversion and settlement must be initiated from the Luxembourg account and referenced to the underlying commercial invoice; no cash or non-bank netting is permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot (T+2) for immediate EUR/USD and EUR/GBP conversion of SaaS receipts
Outright Deliverable FX Forward (EUR/USD) locking conversion rates for maturities up to 12 months
FX Swap (spot versus forward) for short-term liquidity reshaping without increasing structural FX exposure
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS / CCS) to hedge long-term USD-denominated liabilities or subscription receivables
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) permitted only for restricted currencies (for example KRW, TWD, BRL) through approved counterparties and documented under the ISDA 2013 FX Definitions
Vanilla FX Options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) for asymmetric premium-based protection if approved by the treasury policy

All OTC instruments must be executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and the 2013 ISDA FX Definitions; as a non-financial counterparty below the EMIR clearing thresholds (NFC-), the Luxembourg SARL is exempt from mandatory clearing and bilateral margin rules, but remains subject to EMIR trade reporting to an ESMA-registered trade repository, which may be delegated to the counterparty bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (annual financial statements and annexes) with the RCS and publication in the RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS / RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; approval must occur no later than six months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, practical filing deadline is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory fine up to EUR 5,000, coercive fines (astreinte) ordered by court, and prolonged default may trigger court-ordered dissolution and strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (RBE annual declaration/confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March; any shareholding or UBO change occurring during the year must additionally be filed with the RBE within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per failure; repeated non-compliance can lead to criminal referral and, ultimately, court-ordered sanctions or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (IRC) and municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal, ICC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, file by 30 June (paper) or 31 December (electronic) of the year following the relevant tax year; extensions may be granted on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment by the tax office, late-payment interest, late-filing surcharges, and enforced recovery; responsible officers may face joint liability for uncollected taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual corporate income tax return; generally 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year SARL.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment, late-payment interest, fines for incomplete or inaccurate declarations, and enforced tax collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises is compulsory when the SARL exceeds two of the following thresholds at two consecutive balance-sheet dates: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and an average annual workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities and CSSF-supervised financial vehicles.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Commercial Code; consolidated accounts of entities falling within its scope may use IFRS-EU, but private SARL statutory accounts are prepared in Luxembourg GAAP and denominated in EUR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year the SARL must certify or update the beneficial-owner information held in the RBE no later than 31 March. Share transfers or any change in ownership/UBO trigger a separate RBE filing within one month. The registered agent should verify the pre-populated RBE record against the share register and file the confirmation before the deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (part sociale/share quota register)
Minute Book (shareholders' meeting and board minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 per year (if the statutory audit threshold is met)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% of qualifying investments), and participation exemption for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg tax administration's eTVA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; extensions may be granted upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, address, registration number, fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg permanent establishment details if applicable; otherwise, indicate non-resident status and local tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net result after adjustments for tax provisions, depreciation, and exempt income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source income attributable to the PE; apply treaty provisions to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions (e.g., IP box deduction, participation exemption, notional interest deduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions directly related to Luxembourg-source income; maintain supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 1001-A for foreign tax credit; ensure treaty eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of related-party transactions (transfer pricing disclosure)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete if transactions with related parties exceed €450,000; attach TP documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from €250 to €2,500 per return, plus daily surcharge of 0.6% of the tax due (capped at 10%). Non-filing may trigger administrative fines and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the parent holds at least 10% of the subsidiary for 12 consecutive months; also reduced under tax treaties).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the residence state and Form 7 (withholding tax exemption request) to the Luxembourg tax administration prior to payment. The TRC must be certified and include the fiscal year of entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest is 15%. Under tax treaties, rates may be reduced to 0% (e.g., EU Interest and Royalties Directive) or 5% depending on the treaty and ownership thresholds.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed €450,000; Master File required if group consolidated turnover exceeds €50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to entities engaged in certain activities (including holding, financing, and IP). A SARL must demonstrate adequate substance (physical office, qualified staff, decision-making in Luxembourg) to avoid being classified as a shell company, which could trigger penalties and recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, falsification of accounts, or use of artificial arrangements to avoid Luxembourg corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties of 10% to 200% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company without real presence, staff, or decision-making in Luxembourg, particularly for holding or IP activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and penalties up to €250,000; potential forced liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they fail to ensure substance; may face disqualification and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (customer due diligence, record-keeping, reporting suspicious transactions) despite being a low-risk SaaS entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable for AML breaches, including imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for software licensing, management fees, or financing that deviate from arm's length, resulting in profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties of 10% to 50% of the additional tax due, and interest on underpayments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-arm's length pricing; potential criminal charges for tax fraud.
